meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جلود.

examples.trans: This is a small brown leather notebook.
The leather bag is heavy and sturdy.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رجالية, plural: —).

examples.trans: We found a large pair of men's shoes in the bag.
A dark grey men's coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رمادية, plural: رماديين).

examples.trans: He is wearing a dark grey coat.

examples.text: بدنا نحمي بيتنا من المكاتب الرمادية.
examples.trans: We want to protect our house from grey offices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

شاء.gloss: to will (إن شاء الله God willing)

meanings.en: to will (إن شاء الله God willing)
meanings.note: Used in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase إن شاء الله ('God willing / hopefully').

examples.trans: Everything alright, hopefully?
You will arrive safely, God willing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضواو.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقعد, بيقعد).

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقلق, بيقلق).

examples.text: لا تقلقي يا مدام، هلا بنشوف البطاقة.
examples.trans: Do not worry, ma'am, we will check the tag right now.
We worried a little when the bus ran late.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كنزات.

examples.trans: Wear a warm wool cardigan in the evening.
He folded the grey sweaters inside the bag.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلبس, بيلبس).

examples.text: أنا أكيد ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four!

examples.text: لبس معطفه قبل ما يطلع بالمطر.
examples.trans: He put on his coat before going out in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مربوطة, plural: مربوطين).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag tied to the handle.
The red ribbon is tied securely.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مقاسات.

examples.trans: This size fits you perfectly.
The shop sells all pipe sizes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملفوفة, plural: ملفوفين).

examples.text: شو هاد الشي الملفوف بورق أبيض؟
examples.trans: What is this thing wrapped in white paper?
The parcel is wrapped with great care.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

هيك.gloss: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)

meanings.en: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'like this / that way' (عشان هيك 'that is why', مع هيك 'even so').

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian/Levantine encourager ('come on! / let us...!').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.
